headline: INPEX begins first CO2 injection at Kashiwazaki Hydrogen Park
summary: INPEX commenced CO2 injection into the depleted Higashi-Kashiwazaki gas field (Niigata) as part of Japan's first fully integrated blue hydrogen/ammonia production-and-usage demonstration, capturing CO2 with BASF/JGC HiPACT technology; it targets at least 2.5 Mtpa of CO2 injection by 2030.
co2crc_note: Live demonstration of depleted-reservoir CO2 storage tied to blue ammonia in Japan — a key prospective customer for Australian CO2 export and a direct analogue for Australia's blue-ammonia-plus-CCS pathway.
extractor_note: Injection commenced 27 Aug JST; wide coverage 28 Aug (Melbourne). capacity_mtpa 2.5 = INPEX's stated 2030 CO2 injection target, not current rate (current H2 output ~700 t/yr).

headline: Woodside's Browse CCS cleared for full assessment under the amended EPBC Act
summary: The federal Environment Minister determined that Woodside's resubmitted Browse CCS referral will be assessed wholly under the amended EPBC Act 1999, restoring a defined federal assessment pathway; the scheme would inject CO2 into the offshore Calliance Storage Formation (permit G-8-AP) and cut project emissions by ~53 Mt CO2e vs a 2019 Scope 1 baseline.
co2crc_note: Regulatory progress on a flagship Australian offshore CCS project central to the contested Browse gas development; directly relevant to CO2CRC's Australian storage focus.
extractor_note: Procedural assessment determination, not FID (commitment_status announced). 53 Mt CO2e is a lifetime reduction estimate, not additive; capacity_mtpa 4.0 = Woodside's proposed injection rate (~4 Mtpa) reported previously.

headline: Pertamina identifies 13 CCS/CCUS study locations across Indonesia (~7.3 Gt potential)
summary: At Jakarta's International & Indonesia CCS Forum, Pertamina said it has identified ~13 CCS/CCUS study locations across Sumatra, Java, Kalimantan and Sulawesi with combined storage potential of ~7.3 Gt, headlined by the Asri Basin hub (up to ~2.9 Gt), under its Dual Growth Strategy toward net zero by 2060.
co2crc_note: A concrete storage pipeline behind Indonesia's regional-hub push — Australia's most direct competitor/collaborator for storage-constrained Asian CO2.
extractor_note: 7.3 Gt (and Asri Basin 2.9 Gt) is a cumulative storage RESOURCE estimate, not an event/annual capacity, so capacity_mtpa left null per golden rule. Feasibility-stage study identification (instrument_type R&D).

headline: Tangguh CCUS set to become the first CCS project registered under the Indonesia-Japan Joint Crediting Mechanism
summary: The Indonesia-Japan JCM Joint Committee approved the Ofaweri decarbonisation initiative built on the BP-operated Tangguh CCUS project (West Papua) to advance as a JCM project, making it the first CCUS project registered under the bilateral crediting framework; it follows a BP/Mitsubishi Research Institute METI-commissioned JCM CCUS methodology study.
co2crc_note: A working template for monetising cross-border CCS via a bilateral carbon-credit framework — directly relevant to Australia's transboundary CO2 storage ambitions under London Protocol Article 6 arrangements.
extractor_note: Cross-border/transboundary crediting milestone (Indonesia captures/stores, credits shared with Japan). Registration approval, not FID or credit issuance yet (commitment_status announced).

headline: Indonesia positions itself as an Asia-Pacific CCS hub, flagging up to US$43bn of investment potential
summary: Coverage from the 4th International & Indonesia CCS Forum framed Indonesia as an emerging regional CCS hub, with the Indonesia CCS Center and Pertamina Hulu Energi pitching a cross-border storage build-out that could attract up to ~US$43bn of investment, create ~170,000 jobs/yr and lift GDP by ~0.8-1%, leveraging national storage potential above 400 Gt.
co2crc_note: Indonesia is Australia's most direct competitor and potential collaborator for storage-constrained Asian CO2 (Japan, South Korea, Singapore); its hub economics reset the regional benchmark.
extractor_note: US$43bn is a projected economy-wide investment potential (market-aggregate), not a discrete committed sum, so amount is null and commitment_status na per golden rules. 400 Gt is a national storage resource.

headline: Oil & gas companies remain the key adopters of CCUS despite project-delivery challenges - GlobalData
summary: A GlobalData analysis finds >70% of operational and upcoming capture facilities (by count) are tied to energy assets as of June 2026, with oil-and-gas players still driving CCUS around LNG, refining, hydrogen and upstream; the operational base is ~140 projects and ~62 Mtpa cumulative capacity, most future capacity stuck at feasibility/FEED, with shared pipelines, shipping and storage hubs flagged as the critical unlock.
co2crc_note: Global read on where the CCS pipeline is actually converting from FEED to construction — useful context for benchmarking Australian projects against the worldwide operational base.
extractor_note: 62 Mtpa is the global cumulative operational capacity (market-aggregate/cumulative), not a discrete new event capacity, so capacity_mtpa and amount left null per golden rules. Analyst report (commitment_status na).
